cases.input: Cross-session persona and diary for DeepSeek Harness: a local gate decides whether a turn is worth remembering, then one extra model call turns it into a first-person diary entry plus an impression of the user, where every impression carries the specific moment that produced it. Later conversations inject about 2000 tokens of that as a self-memory block in three registers: a persona core, a section for judgements the model wrote itself, and the diary. There is a tool for the model to record a judgement in its own words, and a plain markdown hand-note file the human can write into which the plugin only ever reads. A sidebar panel lets you read, forget or export the archive, and forgetting demotes an entry rather than deleting it, so an old one still surfaces on a strong topical match. Local-only, secrets are stripped before anything is sent, and the archive is a plain folder you can read, edit or carry to another account. Zero runtime dependencies, no build step.

cases.input: Exposes the models already configured in DeepSeek Harness through an OpenAI-compatible gateway, so other local projects can call them with any standard OpenAI client. Multiple provider candidates share one named group with ordered, balanced or random dispatch; upstream failures before any output switch to the next candidate transparently, and rate-limited requests are retried after the provider's backoff. Per-candidate call statistics (attempts, answers, failures, token/TTFT totals) appear as badges in the settings page, and daily aggregates persist to a local file with a 30-day heatmap and trend view. Until you create a key in the UI, the endpoint accepts calls from anyone who can reach it; keys (stored as SHA-256 hashes) then turn authentication on, and the endpoint stays locked even after the last key is revoked. Exposing the optional LAN listener without a key leaves the port open to the whole network. Runs on DSH 0.1.2-rc.1 through 0.1.7-alpha.1 and later.

cases.input: Keeps one reasoning-only turn from making an entire session unusable. When a turn produces no visible text and no tool call, the assistant message is persisted empty, the gateway then rejects every later request in that session with 'content or tool_calls must be set', and the session is dead with no way back through chat. This plugin registers a single llm/stream waterfall listener and, only when the turn carried nothing visible, injects a small text block immediately before the terminal finish, so the persisted message is never empty. Ships the fixture DSH's own mock cannot express (a strictly reasoning-only SSE server, since llm-mock-server forbids an empty successText and always appends text after reasoning), plus an end-to-end reproduction that replays a real persisted session through DSH's own serializeMessages. Preventive, not a repair. Zero dependencies, one file, no process or filesystem access.

cases.input: macOS only: holds a PreventUserIdleSystemSleep assertion (caffeinate -i -w <host pid>) while any DSH session runs, and releases it when the last one stops, so a long turn is not cut off by idle sleep. The display may still turn off. It keeps holding through the maintenance phase, where Agent.status reports idle and a long manual /compact runs, via the compaction/start and compaction/end events. It reconciles against ctx.agents.list() every 60s, so a session already running when the plugin is hot-reloaded is picked up at once instead of at the next turn boundary. A failed hold retries with exponential backoff capped at 60s and never gives up; release escalates from SIGTERM to SIGKILL after 2s, and -w lets caffeinate exit by itself if the host dies. No browser half — configured through the profile patch. 51 tests, including two that read pmset -g assertions on real hardware.

cases.input: Sit-and-water reminder for DeepSeek Harness, with a cat that sits in the corner of the Web GUI. A focus cycle of 30-90 minutes ends in a centered overlay plus a triple chime that gets you up to walk and drink; the later button answers with one real sourced case about prolonged sitting and one about dehydration (built-in library of 17 entries, each with publisher, date and a link to the original); stopping produces a session report with worked time, completed rounds, successful interruptions, snoozes, suggested drinks and a good/mid/bad grade. cases.input: Skill that fact-checks a claim against the open web rather than model memory: it splits the claim into independently checkable fact points, routes each point to the primary-source ladder for its domain (policy, academic, medical, financial, disaster and accidents, food safety, science, education, sports, entertainment, judicial, and more), searches domestic and international ecosystems in parallel, fetches primary pages, grades sources by type, re-searches with debunking keywords, and reports conclusion-first with a full URL and citation position behind every statement, keeping unverified and undecidable points separate from confirmed ones. cases.input: Computer Use for macOS desktop applications: reads any app's accessibility tree as text with element indices, then clicks, types, pastes, scrolls, drags, selects text and sets values through it, plus screenshots read back as images. Driven by a persistent JavaScript REPL — the agent gets two tools (`js`, `js_reset`) and calls an `sky` API inside them, so state survives between calls and the tool schema stays fixed as capabilities grow. Accessibility trees come back as diffs after the first read; actions address elements by index and indices from a stale read are refused rather than misapplied; typing waits for keyboard focus and reads the field back; paste restores the clipboard. Requires macOS 14.4+, Accessibility permission (Screen Recording only for screenshots) and Node 20+; ships a prebuilt native module, so nothing compiles at install time.

cases.input: Lists the Markdown documents, images and video that already exist anywhere in the session workspace in the DSH sidebar, ranked by relevance to the current conversation: recent messages are matched locally against document title, summary and body with IDF weighting, with no model calls and no network. cases.input: Read-only Skill inspector for DeepSeek Harness. It shows which Skills a conversation actually loaded — from observed loading evidence only — and which Skills the current environment can discover, and gives each Skill a detail page that keeps its declaration apart from its run: the body split into structure, declared workflow and progressive disclosure, the run logic read from local receipts, and the per-step evidence behind each claim. Evidence is never promoted into a conclusion — a step with no observed evidence is reported as such, not as executed or not executed — and the run's instruction hash is shown beside the current definition as match, mismatch or unavailable. It also reads the body, offers a Chinese reading version, and can clone a Skill into a local copy. It never writes back to the source Skill and never runs its scripts.

cases.input: Same-origin in mechanism with the two loudest lines in context compression. The code-skeleton gate follows the skeletonization approach of Headroom (Apache-2.0), whose published headline is 20% fewer tokens for coding agents and 60–95% fewer tokens for JSON, same answers. The estimator channel follows TokenPilot (arXiv:2606.17016), which reports up to 60% lower cost for long-session agents. Both figures are theirs, quoted as-is; this plugin ships no benchmark of its own and claims no reduction of its own. What it adds for DeepSeek Harness: choose a compression profile, set the Auto Compact trigger level and toggle code-skeleton compression from one settings section, with exact DeepSeek V4 tokenizer measurement, same-revision count verification, and fail-open behaviour that keeps the original tool results on unsupported models.

cases.input: Live token cost for every chat in the DSH Web UI: the chat, its subagents and the whole session tree, priced from a bundled models.dev snapshot of seven providers and 139 priced models, with cache read and write rates wherever the provider publishes them and DeepSeek from its own peak and off-peak table. cases.input: Cross-workspace worker fleets: one orchestrating session spawns named worker sessions in other project workspaces, queues or steers tasks into them, watches them in the background via a real host job, and collects their reports. Worker completions deliver themselves to the orchestrator's session rather than needing to be polled, so an idle orchestrator still reacts. Escalations and failed workers deliver by steer when the orchestrator is mid-turn and by queue when it is idle; a turn that ends without a report counts as a failure and the worker is replaced after a configurable limit. The roster persists to disk and each worker session carries a durable title, so a restart neither loses the fleet nor spawns duplicate sessions. Ships five agent presets at full plugin parity with the standard preset.

cases.input: Keeps a pool of models and routes every agent step to one of them with its reasoning effort set — configured by clicking in the composer, no JSON needed. cases.input: Instance manager for DSH Web: a Mini Utility Dock panel that lists every local dsh web instance the machine can see (port, PID, uptime, live session count, resident memory, version), starts a new instance on an automatically picked free port in 3080-3129 or on a port you name, opens a row in a new tab, and stops one or all of them through that instance’s own graceful shutdown (appExit). cases.input: Browser provider for DeepSeek Harness: hand it a web task — open a page, click, type, fill a form, read what is on it — and it drives a real browser step by step, seeing an indexed table of what can be done on the current page instead of raw HTML or screenshots. Each step is one bundled-Jev decision rather than a full model turn (1.1 s median per step versus 2.8–3.6 s for chat-model turns in the repo benchmark), and the main conversation receives only the conclusion, so its context does not grow with the page. cases.input: Layered cross-session memory for DSH that pushes only what changed - the first round injects every active entry, later rounds push only added / updated / removed ones, and nothing at all is injected when nothing changed, with keys that merely repeat an entry id left out of the text so the baseline is about 26% smaller. Facts and decisions carry semantic keys (one active truth per key), the model may only write to an inbox that a human promotes, an entry can carry a review date that raises a one-time reminder when due, and search is relevance-ranked with journal lines down-weighted and Chinese matched by bigram. A sidebar tab tells the lifecycle story instead of listing files - entries are grouped by stage (awaiting confirmation / in use / archived) along four axes (topic - one level, human-assigned, type, tag, date), each group can be ticked for batch promote / withdraw / archive / restore / delete / assign topic, and topics can be renamed store-wide or searched on their own. The archived stage reads in three levels - the category says why an entry left (distilled into the docs / useless for good / not needed right now, the first two being defaults you can add to), below it the entry topic stays collapsed until you click it, and entries with no topic sit right under the category. The tab also shows the global and workspace instruction files plus the current injection size. A zero-dependency CLI ships with it, so the store is usable without DSH.
cases.expected: layered cross session memory for dsh that pushes only what changed the first round injects every active entry later rounds push only added updated removed ones and nothing at all is injected when nothing changed with keys that merely repeat an entry id left out of the text so the baseline is about 26 smaller facts and decisions carry semantic keys one active truth per key the model may only write to an inbox that a human promotes an entry can carry a review date that raises a one time reminder when due and search is relevance ranked with journal lines down weighted and chinese matched by bigram a sidebar tab tells the lifecycle story instead of listing files entries are grouped by stage awaiting confirmation in use archived along four axes topic one level human assigned type tag date each group can be ticked for batch promote withdraw archive restore delete assign topic and topics can be renamed store wide or searched on their own the archived stage reads in three levels the category says why an entry left distilled into the docs useless for good not needed right now the first two being defaults you can add to below it the entry topic stays collapsed until you click it and entries with no topic sit right under the category the tab also shows the global and workspace instruction files plus the current injection size a zero dependency cli ships with it so the store is usable without dsh
